ratings_why.fun: Counting to exactly 7 or deliberately boiling over is a real turn-by-turn puzzle, and the board visibly grows from End of Turn and Flare buffs; the early game is thin and the arithmetic can tire.
ratings_why.distinct: One Lamp dial with two opposite builds (stop at the mark vs go over) plays unlike today's tribes, though it is a known push-your-luck borrow and a spell-count resource underneath.

verdict_why: v2 cleared the timing and wording gaps; every card now reads and works as written, and further passes would mostly reshuffle numbers.

points.text: Lamplit Compounder reads Heat after the cast, so a cast that Flares pays +0. That works as written but will surprise players; the Heat preview on hover should show it, or the card could say it reads Heat before any Flare.
Old Carbonaria needs a second counter, Heat gained this turn, next to Heat you have. Show both on the Lamp dial, or the card reads as a guess.

The fantasy comes through in play: moths drawn to the flame, the Old Lady snuffing, eyespots draining Attack, Pavonia who never eats and can't gain stats. Keep names tied to these habits in any later pass.
The Alchymist moves the mark to 3, which silently retargets The Spectacle and The Old Lady. Showing the Flashpoint as a moved number on the dial would make that combo legible.

standouts.why: The Old Lady is a clean safety valve and a sell decision in one line, and the moth-snuffer image fits.
Atropos counting as every tribe and stealing a shop unit on a Flare is the death's-head hive thief, read at a glance.
Dame Pavonia can't gain stats but doubles End of Turn effects: the mouthless emperor told by rules alone.

weakest.why: The Uncertain is mostly a Phial dispenser; its random Stoke adds a roll but little to look at on the board.
Skep Pilferer is a stock spell-to-gold engine with a hive-robbing name and little moth in what it does.
The Herald is a battery: Stoke 3 each turn, with the Tier-up Stoke as its only moment.

flags.note: With Dame Pavonia and many Flares, Carbonaria's board-wide payout runs far above the Tier 6 top end; the designer already names it.
At Flashpoint 3 with Eyed Hawk-moth and Burnt-Ring Senior, a fight can Flare every few hits and stack permanent buffs mid-fight.
Its payout drops to 0 on a cast that Flares; players may read that as a bug unless the UI previews it.
